<jats:title>A<jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>
                     </jats:title><jats:p>We consider supersymmetric domain walls of four-dimensional <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \mathcal{N} $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> = 1 Sp(<jats:italic>N</jats:italic>) SQCD with <jats:italic>F</jats:italic> = <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> + 1 and <jats:italic>F</jats:italic> = <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> + 2 flavors.</jats:p><jats:p>First, we study numerically the differential equations defining the walls, classifying the solutions. When <jats:italic>F</jats:italic> = <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> + 2, in the special case of the parity-invariant walls, the naive analysis does not provide all the expected solutions. We show that an infinitesimal deformation of the differential equations sheds some light on this issue.</jats:p><jats:p>Second, we discuss the 3<jats:italic>d</jats:italic><jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \mathcal{N} $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> = 1 Chern-Simons-matter theories that should describe the effective dynamics on the walls. These proposals pass various tests, including dualities and matching of the vacua of the massive 3<jats:italic>d</jats:italic> theory with the 4<jats:italic>d</jats:italic> analysis. However, for <jats:italic>F</jats:italic> = <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> +2, the semiclassical analysis of the vacua is only partially successful, suggesting that yet-to-be-understood strong coupling phenomena are into play in our 3<jats:italic>d</jats:italic><jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \mathcal{N} $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> = 1 gauge theories.</jats:p>
